{{Short description|Science lectures}}

The '''George Gamow Memorial Lectures''' are an annual series of lectures at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]], named in honor of the physicist and science popularizer [[George Gamow]], author of ''[[One Two Three... Infinity]]'' and the ''[[Mr Tompkins]]'' series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The George Gamow Memorial Lecture Series |date=7 April 2016 |url=https://www.colorado.edu/physics/events/outreach/george-gamow-memorial-lecture-series}}</ref>

==Background==
The lectures were established by Gamow's widow, [[Barbara Perkins Gamow]], and the University's Department of Physics in 1971, to "promote public understanding of the nature and role of science." In 1975, Mrs. Gamow included in her will an endowment to maintain the lectures. The George Gamow lecturers have included 27 [[List of Nobel laureates|Nobel Laureates]] in the sciences. Lectures are held at the university's Macky Auditorium, and are free and open to the public.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brennan |first=Charlie |date=April 26, 2017 |title=George Gamow Memorial Lecture on tap at CU Boulder |work=[[Daily Camera]] |url=https://www.dailycamera.com/2017/04/26/george-gamow-memorial-lecture-on-tap-at-cu-boulder/}}</ref>

[[Frances Arnold]], Nobel Laureate in Chemistry, 2018, was to lecture on “Innovation by Evolution: Bringing New Chemistry to Life”<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fifty-Third Gamow Lecture March 31, 2020 to Feature Nobel Laureate Frances Arnold |url=https://www.colorado.edu/physics/2019/04/03/fifty-third-gamow-lecture-march-31-2020-feature-nobel-laureate-frances-arnold}}</ref> but her lecture was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite news |title=53rd Gamow Memorial Lecture at CU Boulder postponed due to COVID-19 coronavirus |work=[[Colorado Arts and Sciences Magazine]] |url=https://www.colorado.edu/asmagazine/2020/03/12/53rd-gamow-memorial-lecture-cu-boulder-postponed-due-covid-19-coronavirus}}</ref> In 2024, the Lectures resumed with Dr. [[Andrea Ghez]], Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2020.
